people.jude-letter.role: Writer who calls himself a servant of Jesus Christ
people.jude-letter.meaning: He plans to write about a shared salvation. He writes instead to urge his readers to defend the faith. He warns of men who crept in and denies their teaching. He ends with orders. Build yourselves up and pray. Show mercy to some, and snatch others from the fire.
people.jesus.role: Master and Lord, source of mercy
people.jesus.meaning: Jude says certain men deny him as the only Master and Lord. Readers are told to keep in God’s love and look for his mercy. That mercy leads to eternal life.
people.moses.role: Man whose body Michael and the devil argued over
people.moses.relations: Michael, the archangel, argued with the devil about his body.
people.moses.meaning: Jude says Michael argued with the devil about the body of Moses. Michael did not dare to curse the devil. He said, “May the Lord rebuke you!” Jude says the men he warns about speak evil of what they do not know.
people.cain.role: Man whose way Jude warns against
people.cain.meaning: Jude says the men he warns about went in the way of Cain. Jude does not say here what Cain did. The warning ends in woe.
people.balaam.role: Man whose error was done for hire
people.balaam.relations: Jude names him with Cain and Korah.
people.balaam.meaning: Jude says the men he warns about ran in the error of Balaam for hire. The phrase “for hire” ties his error to payment. Jude gives no story of Balaam here.
people.korah.role: Man whose rebellion ended in destruction
people.korah.relations: Jude names him with Cain and Balaam.
people.korah.meaning: Jude says the men he warns about perished in Korah’s rebellion. Jude gives no story of Korah here. The name shows that rebellion ends in ruin.
people.enoch.role: Seventh from Adam, who prophesied judgment
people.enoch.relations: Jude calls him the seventh from Adam.
people.enoch.meaning: Jude says Enoch prophesied about the men he warns about. Enoch said the Lord came with ten thousands of his holy ones. The Lord comes to judge all the ungodly for their works and words.
people.adam.role: First man, named to place Enoch
people.adam.relations: Jude calls Enoch the seventh from Adam.
people.adam.meaning: Jude names Adam only once. He uses the name to say Enoch was the seventh from Adam. Jude tells no story about Adam.
places.sodom.summary: Jude recalls Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them in chapter 1. They gave themselves over to sexual immorality and strange flesh. Jude says they are shown as an example and suffer the punishment of eternal fire.
places.sodom.limits: The site is disputed. The marker shows a region, not a confirmed city.
sources.web.summary: The full text of Jude is the main text for the close readings.
sources.web.limits: Jude names himself as the letter’s writer. The text does not tie him to a Gospel relative or an apostle. Authorship, dates, Greek forms, and the exact opponents were not checked independently. The earlier sources for the Michael and Enoch accounts were not checked either. Sodom is only a marker for a disputed region.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-49.summary: The lesson links Jude’s warning images to resisting false teaching and showing compassion.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-49.limits: Coverage follows what the lesson says about Jude. Linked reference entries and Restoration passages were not checked independently. The idea of apostasy is Church teaching.
sources.usccb-jude.summary: The introduction says Jude changed his subject to answer harmful teachers urgently.
sources.usccb-jude.limits: This is the introduction’s own reading. Historical identities, proposals about the author, dates, and the opponents were not checked independently. Borrowing between texts and the earlier works it cites were not checked either.
sources.atlas.summary: This atlas from the Church shows the wider setting and marks some disputed places.
sources.atlas.limits: Treat the place labels as background. The linked atlas also has Latter-day Saint commentary.
sources.atlas-canaan.summary: This atlas from the Church shows towns and regions in Canaan.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: The coordinates are estimates for display. A town marker does not prove each event in the text.
chapters.*.mapNote: The Sodom marker shows a disputed region, not a confirmed city.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: Jude names no travel route, so the map draws none.
